name: Pork with Bamboo Shoot (Gahori Khorisa)
instructions: 1. Clean and cut the pork into medium-sized pieces.
2. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan until it smokes slightly.
3. Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cooking for a minute.
5. Add the pork pieces and turmeric powder, frying on medium-high heat until the fat renders.
6. Add the fermented bamboo shoots and salt, stir-frying for 5-7 minutes.
7. Add enough water to submerge the meat, cover, and simmer on low heat until the pork is tender.
8. Adjust seasoning with black pepper and serve hot with steamed rice.
description: Gahori Khorisa is a quintessential dish of the Assamese tribal cuisine, particularly popular among the Bodo and Mishing communities. The use of 'Khorisa' (fermented bamboo shoot) provides a distinct tangy depth to the rich, fatty pork, reflecting the region's tradition of using locally foraged ingredients.
